edition.notes: Swete prints the Vatican text as the larger upper text and the materially different Sinaitic Tobit in full beneath it in smaller type, with verses aligned as nearly as possible. His description of the Sinaitic form as having a secondary character is an editorial judgment of this dated edition, not adopted by Triptych. This controls the two printed Greek forms and their boundaries, not a modern critical apparatus, manuscript images, or adjudication among recensions.
edition.publication: Edited by Henry Barclay Swete, Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, second edition, 1896
edition.title: The Old Testament in Greek according to the Septuagint, volume 2: Tobit

passages.context: Preface p. vii (PDF page 9) and printed pp. 828–835 (PDF pages 844–851) were visually inspected. Swete's larger upper text supplies the Vatican form and his smaller lower text prints the materially different Sinaitic form in full. Both present angelic direction, prayer, marriage, healing, and expulsion within one providential narrative. This verifies the two Greek forms as printed in this edition, not a normal formulary, clinical diagnosis, efficacy, ordinary practice, Christian rite, modern critical adjudication, or operational instruction.
passages.notes: No procedural wording is transcribed. Swete's alignment and editorial hierarchy are features of his 1896 edition; they do not erase recension differences or establish the priority of either form.
